problems: Complete absence of visual identity prevents brand recognition for a Miami-based restaurant
Lack of food photography eliminates the primary emotional trigger for dining decisions
design.quickFix: Launch a basic one-page site featuring high-resolution hero images of signature dishes and the Miami dining atmosphere

problems: No mobile interface exists to capture the high volume of local mobile-first restaurant searches
Inability to access hours or location on mobile leads to immediate user drop-off
mobile.quickFix: Implement a mobile-responsive landing page with a sticky 'Call Now' and 'Get Directions' button

problems: Non-existent infrastructure results in infinite load times for any user attempting to access the business
Zero technical foundation prevents any performance optimization or caching strategies
speed.quickFix: Deploy a lightweight static site generator (like Next.js or Astro) to ensure sub-second load times for the initial page

problems: No indexed pages means GreenStreet is invisible to local search queries for 'restaurants in Miami'
Missing schema markup prevents Google from displaying rich snippets for menu items and ratings
seo.quickFix: Create a dedicated 'Miami Restaurant' landing page with LocalBusiness schema markup including address, hours, and geo-coordinates

problems: No reservation or ordering system exists to convert interest into revenue
Lack of social proof or menu details prevents users from making a commitment to visit
conversion.quickFix: Integrate a third-party reservation widget (like OpenTable or Resy) directly into the homepage header

biggestOpportunity: GreenStreet is currently invisible to the digital dining market in Miami; establishing a basic, mobile-optimized web presence with integrated reservations could capture an estimated 15-20% of local search traffic that is currently being lost to competitors.
